text:
sarah: Heads-up — after landing the AWQ config for mistral-14b (quiet mode) we're seeing a 12–18% P95 tail increase on short-chat traffic. repro script attached in thread.
kevin: Ugh. I noticed higher KV miss spikes in the profiler too. Did we change prefetch affinity or the kernel selector?
sarah: Not intentionally. Change list was: AWQ weights, quant kernel switch to 'fast-int8-matmul', and a small tweak to ropescale (0.95 -> 0.88) to reduce hallucination in our evals.
rav: Can you paste the pprof flameview? quick numbers are enough.
sarah: profiler snapshot (summary):
```
requests: 12k
avg latency: 72ms
p50: 39ms
p95: 124ms (prev 106ms)
kv-cache hit-rate: 87% (prev 94%)
batching efficiency: 0.62 tokens/slot (prev 0.66)
cpu % in matmul kernel: +9%
```
kevin: kv hit-rate drop is big — suggests more prefix churn or KV eviction. Did AWQ change KV size or serialization layout?
anna: AWQ changes shouldn't affect cache keys but different kernel schedule could change micro-batching timing and evictions. Also the ropescale tweak reduces token reuse across similar prompts so cache affinity could drop.
sarah: I ran a quick bisect to isolate: reverted ropescale -> back to 0.95 restores p95 to ~108ms and kv-hit to 92%. Keeping AWQ + fast-int8 still shows ~4% tail delta.
rav: So two contributors: ropescale change (major) + kernel schedule (minor). We should micro-bisect kernel selector next. Can someone run the kernel chooser experiment with these tags:
```
model: mistral-14b
quant: awq
kernels: [fast-int8-matmul, avx-gemm, fallback-ffconv]
batcher: dynbatch-v2
prefetch: affinity=high, throttle=50ms
ropescale: 0.95
```
Run 30k requests sampled from short-chat traffic.
kevin: Running now on canary pool. I also enabled per-request KV debug for a subset and will collect cache keys distribution.
perf-bot: Job queued: job_id=rb-job-8452, canary_pool=canary-a, sampling=1/10, expected_duration=45m
sarah: FYI calibration prompts used for AWQ were 'redwood-calib-3' (50 examples, mixed chat + code). Any chance calibration set pushed logits to favor tokens that change prefix alignment?
anna: Calibration could change weight scaling and therefore numerical roundoff behavior — but it shouldn't affect RoPE keys. Still, small numeric diffs can cascade with KV indexing if we use hash-based bucketization. Are we hashing by float32 vs quantized int?
rav: Good catch — our KV key fingerprinting pipeline used float32 token embeddings pre-quantization for a long time. The AWQ change switches storage to int8 in some paths; we failed to canonicalize keys in the kernel transition. That explains a subset of cache misses.
sarah: So action items: (1) normalize KV keying to use token ids + position + ropescale-quantized (defensive) (2) run kernel chooser experiment (rav/kevin) (3) retune prefetch throttle to avoid micro-evictions (anna) (4) re-run AWQ calibration with 'calib-robust-01' and compare BLEU/accuracy deltas.
kevin: quick note on kernel chooser experiment: add metric 'batching-slot-occupancy' and output per-kernel p95. I'll post results when job completes.
rav: If kernel switch shows nontrivial cost, we can try a hybrid schedule: use avx-gemm for head-dense layers and fast-int8 for mid-layers. Need a small kernel selection policy change in runtime: switch-by-layer-range.
anna: Prefetch throttle hypothesis: with high affinity + aggressive prefetch, the batcher issues more speculative KV inserts which push the warmset into thrash. I propose throttle=120ms on short-chat traffic and see if occupancy improves.
sarah: Also running a small eval on quality deltas from AWQ vs GPTQ on mistral-14b small-set: initial BLANC-style eval shows AWQ -0.7 points vs GPTQ; still within tolerable envelope but combined with ropescale churn it's problematic.
perf-bot: Canary run complete: rb-job-8452 status=done. summary: avx-gemm p95 110ms, fast-int8 p95 118ms, fallback-ffconv 135ms. batching-slot-occupancy: avx-gemm=0.65, fast-int8=0.60. kv-hit-rate: avx-gemm=93%, fast-int8=88%
sarah: Looks like avx-gemm wins in both tail and KV hit-rate. Interesting that fast-int8 degrades cache behavior — likely due to key canonicalization bug + timing.
kevin: I'll roll a patch to canonicalize KV keys (token ids + quant schema) and a kernel policy change to prefer avx-gemm for first 6 layers. Patch: https://coderepo/r/3832
rav: After key canonicalization test on canary, kv-hit jumps to 93.5% with fast-int8 and p95 delta reduces to ~2%. That suggests most of the damage was the keying bug.
anna: Great. After canonicalization + ropescale revert + prefetch throttle bump -> tail back to baseline. We should still plan a controlled rollout for AWQ: new calibration set + kernel policy locked to avx-gemm for first 6 layers for 48hr.
sarah: Agreed. I'll open the rollout ticket and include perf regression gating. Thanks all. :+1:
